verdict.rationale: Twilio's pricing page publishes self-serve, pay-as-you-go pricing ('no subscriptions') with explicit per-participant-minute rates for track recordings and per-composed-minute rates for compositions, so some cost modeling is possible without sales. However, the evidence never shows the core video room rate per participant-minute or any bandwidth-based rate. missing for 10: published core per-participant-minute rate for video rooms, any bandwidth/GB pricing, independent confirmation that no sales contact is needed for modeling.

support.subject: As a founder, usage pricing is published per participant-minute or per unit of bandwidth, so I can model cost without talking to sales

citations.quote: Track recordings cost $0.004 per participant minute and recording compositions (customized video layouts created from individual recordings) cost $0.01 per composed minute.
Only pay for what you use with no subscriptions.
